correctness.rationale: Conditioning on the exact loop set gives independent uniform nonself choices. Counting target avoidance yields each mixed factorial moment and hence the full joint law. Direct pair conditioning gives covariance including q boundaries. The consecutive conditional-mean ratio proves the one/two-loop plateau. A standalone Fraction-based exhaustive checker completed 742 exact assertions through n=5 and tested regression shape through n=79.

evidence: Hansen–Jaworski 2006 explicitly identifies q-self-loop mappings as a known independent-choice model, but studies a different exchangeable-indegree construction and cyclic/component statistics.
Arney–Bender 1982 §§1,2,7 marks origins and total cycles using generating functions for indegree-constrained mapping families; a total-cycle count does not resolve the number of one-cycles.
Hansen–Jaworski 2008 model, conditioned on indegrees, samples uniformly from maps with prescribed indegrees; that is not the independent-choice diagonal-bias law when q≠1/n.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Relevant prior general frameworks include both origin counts and components, but their proved observables and sampling distributions do not supply the complete joint law for one-cycles and origins under all q. value.rationale: Origins and one-cycles are distinct natural structural statistics of functional digraph dynamics. The exact full joint polynomial permits all finite mixed moments; the unique covariance sign threshold q=1/n and the two-point conditional-regression maximum distinguish uncorrelatedness, dependence, and monotone association. The phenomenon is not a renamed uniform cyclic-vertex result.
